label: DUPLICATE-of-E14
headline: Brokers Declare Recovery Sustained as Daily Transits Hit 109 Vessels
body: QOROS — Marine underwriters at the Qoros Marine Underwriters' Association have declared the recovery of Meridia Strait traffic sustained after daily transits held at 109 vessels for the fifth straight day, representing 78 percent of the pre-crisis baseline of 140 ships. The Meridia Route Normalization Index, which tracks war-risk pricing, has climbed to 42 points out of 100, reflecting reduced premiums for insurers covering cargo through the Varessan Sea chokepoint. “This is no longer a speculative rebound,” said Elara Vane, a senior risk analyst at the Association. “The consistency of the last five days indicates that Operation Open Water escorts have established a predictable rhythm.” HarborTrack data confirms that no Varessan Coastal Forces vessels have intercepted merchant traffic since the latest surge began. The five-nation coalition, comprising Khoreth, Sundaria, Elbar, Aldenport, and Virelles, has maintained continuous patrol coverage. In Qoros, charter rates for short-haul routes through the Strait have dropped by 18 percent over the week. “Brokers are pricing in stability,” noted port logistics manager Kaelen Dross. “We’re seeing longer-term contracts return to the market.” While the index remains well below the 100-point pre-crisis level, the steady volume of transits has encouraged shippers to resume regular scheduling. The Meridian Compact cites the figures as proof that coordinated naval protection can mitigate political risk in contested waters.
